option_relations.rationale: Optic nerve astrocytoma is a tumor of the optic nerve, while Branch Retinal Artery Occlusion is a vascular event affecting the retina. There is no direct clinical relationship between the two.
Primary optic nerve glioma is a tumor of the optic nerve, while Branch Retinal Artery Occlusion is a vascular event affecting the retina. There is no direct clinical relationship between the two.

Optic nerve glioma (astrocytoma) is a tumor of the optic nerve, while Branch Retinal Artery Occlusion is a vascular event affecting the retina. There is no direct clinical relationship between the two.

Glioblastoma with optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension is a malignant brain tumor affecting the optic nerve and eye, while Branch Retinal Artery Occlusion is a vascular event affecting the retina. There is no direct clinical relationship between the two.
